name: The Lookout
description: Our high room, looking east across the harbour mouth.
longDescription: Climb to the top floor for uninterrupted water and weather. The Lookout is bright at dawn, quiet after dark, and made for slow cups of tea in the window seat.
imageAlt: Calm guest room with white linen and a wide sea-facing window
goodToKnow: Two flights of stairs and no lift. Morning light arrives early in midsummer.

name: The Boat House
description: A ground-floor room with its own door onto the old slipway garden.
longDescription: The Boat House sits closest to the garden and has the easiest access. Limewashed walls, a broad bed and a sheltered bench outside make it our room for unhurried weekends.
imageAlt: Textured coastal bedroom with pale walls and warm wood furniture
goodToKnow: The garden path is gently sloped but laid with old stone; ask us about access needs before booking.

name: The Salt Store
description: A compact room under the eaves, warm with evening sun.
longDescription: Once used to dry nets and store salt, this is the smallest room in the house. Its pitched ceiling, old rafters and west window give it the feeling of a well-kept hideaway.
imageAlt: Small inviting bedroom beneath timber rafters with rust-coloured textiles
goodToKnow: Sloped ceilings make this room less suitable for very tall guests.
